the ultra-intense fields that are observed in the quiet Sun are a natural outcome of nonlinear interactions between convection and a weak magnetic field, and that these fields cannot be explained in the framework of a single flux tube model that is in overall pressure equilibrium.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of magnetic fields with flux densities comparable to the equipartition value, the convective motions are strongly affected by the magnetic fields, and the magnetic fields are strongly affected by convection.
, in the absence of magnetic diffusion, the convective motions can easily generate magnetic fields that are far greater than Be and Bp.
, in a highly supercritical convection, magnetic fields that exceed the equipartition value can be generated and sustained in a self-consistent way.
